risks.description: Pricing and reimbursement pressure, including pricing transparency and access to healthcare
risks.rationale: Growth of healthcare costs, funding restrictions, public controversies regarding pharmaceutical pricing, macroeconomic pressures. IRA in US requiring maximum fair price for Entresto in 2026. EU regulatory developments.

risks.description: Failure to deliver key commercial priorities and successfully launch new products
risks.rationale: Dependence on commercial success of key products. Pressure from competitive products, changes in prescribing habits, slower post-launch adoption, unexpected side effects, supply chain issues, pricing pressure, regulatory proceedings, loss of IP protection.

risks.description: Failure to competitively discover and develop innovative medicines in core therapeutic areas and leveraging technology platforms
risks.rationale: Inherent uncertainty of science, suboptimal internal execution. Challenges in clinical testing, regulatory processes, post-approval activities. Ethical and compliance requirements (patient safety, data privacy, cGCP, data integrity, diversity/inclusion, animal welfare).

risks.description: Expiry, assertion or loss of intellectual property protection
risks.rationale: IP protection varies by product and country. Risk of generic/biosimilar competition, challenges to patents, compulsory licensing, weakening of IP laws, 'at risk' launches. Loss of protection results in significant revenue and income reduction.

risks.description: Failure to identify, execute or realize expected benefits from external business opportunities
risks.rationale: Competitive market for clinical-stage assets and technology platforms. Challenges in identifying opportunities, completing transactions, integrating acquired businesses, achieving expected synergies. Examples: MorphoSys AG, Mariana Oncology, Kate Therapeutics acquisitions in 2024.

risks.description: Failure to meet rapidly evolving environmental, social and governance expectations
risks.rationale: Heightened stakeholder scrutiny on ESG performance. Topics: social inequity, access to medicines, climate change. Impact on reputation, recruitment, retention, operations, financial results, share price. Fast pace of regulatory change.
risks.mitigation: ESG Committee of Executive Committee, Sustainability & ESG Office, ESG strategy and targets tracking

risks.description: May not successfully achieve goals related to Sandoz separation
risks.rationale: Separation completed in 2023. Ongoing obligations under separation agreements. Resource allocation to fulfill obligations. Potential disputes. Risk of tax consequences if spin-off doesn't qualify as tax-neutral for Swiss/US federal income tax.

risks.description: Cybersecurity breaches, data loss and catastrophic loss of IT systems
risks.rationale: Heavy dependence on critical, complex IT systems. Outsourcing to third-party providers including AI services. Vulnerable to cyberattacks (state-sponsored, ransomware, malware). Risk increased due to AI rise and remote working. Past incidents experienced.

risks.description: Inability to identify, attract, develop and retain qualified talent for critical roles
risks.rationale: Competitive market for skilled talent in biology, immunology, chemistry, clinical development, drug manufacturing, data, digital, IT, oncology, advanced therapy platforms. Geographic mobility decreasing. Challenges in key growth markets like US, China.

risks.description: Failure to successfully implement IT strategy may disrupt core business processes
risks.rationale: Current IT systems reaching end of useful life. Implementing companywide IT programs to replace/consolidate systems. Risks: failure to operate as expected, integration failures, delays, data loss, payment/procurement issues, compliance issues, cost overruns.

risks.description: Challenges posed by evolving legal and regulatory requirements, innovative technologies, and societal expectations
risks.rationale: Extensive complex legal/regulatory framework. Evolving interpretations. Subject to legal proceedings (pricing, bribery/corruption, product liability, antitrust, securities, fraud, sales/marketing practices). High costs, management attention. Risk of fines, penalties, exclusion from reimbursement programs.

risks.subcategory: External partner risk and human rights
risks.description: Failure to maintain adequate governance over external partners, and failure of partners to meet obligations
risks.rationale: Reliance on external partners for R&D, manufacturing, warehousing, distribution, finance, sales/marketing, data management. Partners may lack comparable compliance systems. Risks: IP misappropriation, noncompliance with standards (regulatory, environmental, anti-bribery, human rights, quality), supply disruptions, breach of agreement.

risks.description: Inability to ensure proper controls in product development and manufacturing, failure to comply with regulations/standards
risks.rationale: Complex, heavily regulated development/manufacturing. Must comply with regulatory requirements and quality standards. Intensified scrutiny from health authorities. Failure can result in: warning letters, manufacturing suspension, seizure, recalls, approval failures, debarment, patient harm. Advanced therapy platforms (gene/cell, RLT, xRNA) particularly complex.

risks.description: Inability to maintain continuity of product supply
risks.rationale: Technically complex manufacturing, highly specialized raw materials, reliance on single sources. Sterile products, biologics, advanced therapy platforms especially complex. Risk of production failures, supply interruptions, product recalls. Exacerbated during pandemics, macroeconomic factors, geopolitical events (wars).

risks.description: Noncompliance with personal data protection laws and regulations
risks.rationale: Collection/processing of large sets of personal information. Different, potentially conflicting, frequently changing data privacy laws (EU GDPR, Brazil GPDP, China PIPL, US state laws). Stringent requirements, significant penalties for noncompliance. Security breaches could expose personal information. Increasing divergence of legal frameworks.

risks.description: Impact of falsified medicines on patient safety, reputational and financial harm
risks.rationale: Vulnerability of distribution channels to falsified medicines (counterfeit, stolen, tampered, illegally diverted). Patient safety risks, adverse events, reduced confidence in medicines. Reputational/financial harm, potential litigation, direct financial loss when falsified medicines replace genuine sales.

risks.description: Impact of geo- and socio-political threats
risks.rationale: Government shutdowns, administration changes, sovereign risks, acts of war/aggression, terrorist activities. Tariffs, export controls, protectionist measures. Could disrupt supply chain, flow of products, international transactions. Aggressive monetary/fiscal policies to curb inflation. Wars in certain parts of world contributing to high energy costs, inflation.

risks.description: Impact of macroeconomic developments
risks.rationale: Deteriorating macroeconomic/financial conditions. Patients cutting back on prescriptions due to financial constraints. Payers', distributors', suppliers' inability to pay or perform obligations. Weakening growth, unstable markets, rising debt costs increase credit risk. Fiscal pressures on government payers. Slow economic growth, war, high energy costs, inflation straining budgets.

risks.description: Failure to manage physical and transition risks from climate change
risks.rationale: Transition risks: regulatory frameworks, carbon pricing, cost/access to capital. Physical risks: heat, water scarcity, rising sea levels, severe weather events. New regulatory requirements (Switzerland, EU, UK, Australia). May require increased investment in technology to reduce energy, water, GHG emissions. Carbon pricing, climate risk disclosures, zoning/building code changes. Failure to achieve climate commitments could harm reputation.

risks.description: Changes in tax laws or their application
risks.rationale: Multinational operations taxed under various jurisdictions. OECD minimum tax project (Pillar Two) - 15% minimum tax. Switzerland implemented QDMTT for FY2024, income inclusion rule in 2025. EU draft BEFIT directive, draft transfer pricing directive. US IRA: 15% corporate alternative minimum tax, 1% excise tax on stock repurchases. Conflicting claims from tax authorities, transfer pricing disputes. Potential for payments materially different from accrued amounts.

risks.description: Indebtedness could adversely affect operations
risks.rationale: USD 21.4 billion non-current financial debt, USD 8.2 billion current financial debt as of Dec 31, 2024. Requires cash flow dedication to service debt. Rising interest rates may increase payments. Limits flexibility, capital for other uses. Competitive disadvantage vs. less indebted competitors. Difficulty refinancing on reasonable terms.

risks.description: Goodwill and intangible assets resulting in significant impairment charges
risks.rationale: Significant goodwill/intangible assets on balance sheet from acquisitions (Chinook, MorphoSys AG, Mariana Oncology, Kate Therapeutics). If fair value < carrying value, impairment charges incurred. USD 1.4 billion impairment charges in 2024. Regular reviews for impairment. Revisions in estimates/assumptions could result in impairments.

risks.description: Negative effect on financial results due to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations
risks.rationale: Reporting in USD but significant earnings/expenditures in other currencies (especially CHF expenditures > CHF revenue). Exchange rate changes cause increases/decreases in reported sales, costs, earnings, asset/liability values, cash flows. Market risk plus risk of countries taking steps impacting currency values (unconventional monetary policies, tariffs, currency withdrawals). Currency controls in financially challenged/high inflation countries.
risks.mitigation: Measures to reduce/hedge FX risks undertaken but volatility may still negatively impact results

risks.description: Concentration among key customers
risks.rationale: Significant sales to small number of wholesalers, retail chains, purchasing organizations. Top 3 customers: 17%, 13%, 7% of net sales in 2024; 19%, 12%, 7% of trade receivables at Dec 31, 2024. Trend of customer base consolidation. Concentration of credit risk. If major customer experiences financial difficulties, substantial loss of sales, inability to collect amounts owed.

risks.description: Impact of environmental liabilities
risks.rationale: Environmental laws impose obligations to investigate/remediate contaminated sites (from past businesses no longer part of Novartis). Remediation may take many years. Provisions set aside but no guarantee additional costs won't be incurred. Environmental contamination adversely impacting third parties, failure to manage facility safety could result in substantial costs, penalties, increased provisions.

risks.description: Inaccuracies in assumptions/estimates for pension plan and post-employment obligations
risks.rationale: Sponsor pension/post-employment benefit plans covering significant portion of current/former employees. Significant assumptions/estimates required (discount rates, future pension increases, withdrawal/mortality rates). Assumptions may differ materially from actual results due to changing market/economic conditions, withdrawal rates, life spans. Differences could materially affect equity, require additional pension fund contributions.

ai_positioning.summary_fr: Novartis intègre l'intelligence artificielle de manière croissante dans ses activités de R&D pour évaluer plus efficacement de nouvelles molécules, accélérer les délais de développement de médicaments et optimiser la conception de médicaments et les processus d'essais cliniques. L'entreprise s'appuie également sur des fournisseurs tiers pour des services d'IA dans son infrastructure IT. L'IA est considérée comme stratégiquement importante pour rester compétitif, mais l'échec de sa mise en œuvre pourrait désavantager Novartis et impacter sa productivité.

events_milestones.description: Novartis AG incorporated on February 29, 1996 under laws of Switzerland
Predecessor companies Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG merged into Novartis AG, creating Novartis
Completed 100% spin-off of Sandoz (generics and biosimilars division) into new Swiss publicly traded independent company
Closed acquisitions of MorphoSys AG, Mariana Oncology, and Kate Therapeutics
Entered into several strategic partnerships for development and commercialization of innovative products across core therapeutic areas
Acceded to 'maximum fair price' under US IRA for Entresto for 2026 to avoid fines or removal from Medicare/Medicaid (August 2024)
Dr. Giovanni Caforio scheduled to join Board as Non-Executive Chair (after shareholder approval), succeeding Joerg Reinhardt who steps down after 12 years
